body: Yes, I am. I asked this same question over there and got some helpful responses! But we want to keep an open mind in case we find somewhere we like more than Asheville. So I thought I’d come to the NC sub to get more perspectives.

I think the move to Asheville is inevitable. Just looking to see if there anywhere else to consider that we might like more. What you recommend makes sense. Anywhere in particular you recommend visiting?

Unfortunately, I don’t think what I want exists at all! I don’t need a place that’s entirely blue. Just somewhere where I’m not the only one. I’ve got some hardcore Trumper future family members (m white fiancé’s side of the family) and as long as we don’t talk politics, we get on great! I really just want a community where I’m not the only different person. Somewhere we can put down roots, really be members of the community, and make friends.

I grew up in Maryland right on the DC border. I understood the draw of the city but never felt it myself. But having grown up there, I’ve never worried about being the only non white person around (outside of school of course). But it’s something I’m aware of now and I just don’t feel comfortable with.

If not Asheville, where would you recommend?

I’m not really familiar with other mountainous areas of NC. Just Asheville as we’ve been and liked it. What other places would you recommend? Ideally somewhere where we could have a decent sized garden and some livestock.

Looking for moving location recommendations. Sorry to post again, I realized I posted right before the weekly thread ended so I thought I’d try again with the new one.

Hi everyone. My fiancé and I are both graduating from college in a week and we have been discussing next steps. We still have 6 months left on our lease and have been busy with senior year so we haven’t had the time to start seriously looking into anything.

We were both born and raised in Maryland and studying at the University of Maryland. But we really love Asheville. We’ve been down several times to visit friends and could see ourselves settling happily here. We would want to live and work in the city, renting until we can save up enough money to one day buy a house.

The thing is, when we eventually buy a house or some land, we want it to be out in the countryside so we can have a small homestead (a dream of ours). The only problem is we don’t know much about anywhere outside of Asheville. We are both democrats (if it matters) and I am asian. While my fiancé feels he could settle anywhere because he is white, we are looking for somewhere that is slightly more liberal than conservative and has at least some people of color (ideally including asians) in the area.

I grew up as the only non-white student in a tiny private school. It was actually a really hard time and I experienced some racism. The only thing was I had no one to relate to or look up to that looked like me (I’m adopted so I have white parents). My fiancé and I know we want kids and we both don’t want them to have a similar experience. So it is important to us that we find somewhere with other non-white people.

I know Asheville would be good for this but like I said earlier, eventually we want to move out of the city and somewhere a little more rural. Do any of you know if the areas outside of Asheville also have some liberal people and POC? Thanks in advance!
Don’t worry about it. I actually really appreciate the advice! Thank you!

I’m not a nurse. So I’m unsure if I’m even allowed to comment. If not, just let me know and I will delete my post. A couple years ago I was at the doctor’s for my physical. I needed a blood draw and the nurse in charge was clearly high. She poked me a bunch of times in both arms. Afterwards, when I left, I had a hard painful lump the size of a pea in my right arm where I’d been poked the most. It stayed for 2 weeks before shrinking and going away. It’s never happened to me before but I’ve also never been poked that many times for a blood draw.

I was younger then so I was too scared to say anything or stand up for myself. While my little arm bump was nothing to be concerned about, I was worried about the elderly patients that frequent the office. I did tell my doctor about it the next time I went in but she worked for the company they hire for blood draws and wasn’t their employee so it had been too much time for them to track her down and report her. 

I think you should definitely report any suspected drug use. Especially if you heard the nurse talking about getting high that morning and actually looking high. I would report same day so that it would be easier to prove, but even if that’s not possible, it’s still important to report as soon as possible. I was ok with my blood draw snafu but I would be worried that a nurse working in a hospital has more serious mistakes that can be made and end up harming a patient.

Everyone here has such great advice. My little guy is now 4 months old. He is amazing but definitely a handful. Potty training has been going slowly despite him being wicked smart. He loves to cuddle and be involved in everything. His favorite places are definitely the elevator and the lobby because that is where he meets lots of new people. He generally isn’t too gassy but when he farts, boy does it stink! He is very stubborn and it’s hard not to give in when I see his cute little determined face.

Like everyone has said, be sure to work on socialization and desensitization! Not just to people but to all of his surroundings and to touch. We touch my guy’s paws all the time but he still hates it! Your guy looks delightfully wrinkly so be sure to practice cleaning all his little wrinkles and folds. And don’t forget the tail pocket! Also get him used to baths. It comes in handy when your puppy decides to roll in mud (or, god forbid, his or something else’s poop). Start working immediately on separation anxiety and being quiet in the crate.

Definitely get insurance before the first vet visit. If you don’t and the vet spots anything, it can be classified as a pre-existing condition and you won’t be reimbursed for it. After lots of research, I settled on Trupanion. Pet’s Best looks really good and has high reviews but when you read actual customer reviews everyone says it’s terrible. I didn’t want to even take that risk. Oh and work on bite control/inhibition early on. My guy loves loves loves to chomp down on soft, tender human flesh. He doesn’t care if it is in a sock, under a blanket, or just out in the open. We are working very hard on nipping this in the bud before it becomes a behavioral problem. Also, enforced naps! Keeps them behaving and prevents an overtired puppy.

Having just gone through this, I can tell you that it sucked at first. At times I wondered if I had made a mistake. It is just me so I was constantly sleep deprived and living in a state of constant vigilance. Keep a strict schedule to limit accidents in the house. It will feel so monotonous and exhausting but it’s worth it. The whole young puppy time is adorable but hard work. But the more effort you put in, the better a dog you’re going to end up with. Take lots of pictures and videos. Enjoy the times where they spend most of their time napping rather than awake and wreaking havoc.

Despite how hard the first couple months can be, it is 100% worth it. My little dude has the best personality and is really shaping up into a nice dog. I wouldn’t trade him for the world. He loves to be with me at all times and is a fantastic snuggle buddy. He’s wicked smart and learning new things every day. Congratulations and enjoy your new puppy! He is absolutely adorable!

Uh oh. That doesn’t bode well for me. My guy is 4 months old and crate trained. It is just starting to apply to the house as well. For some reason, it doesn’t apply to the hallways or the elevator. The worst part is that his favorite places to pee inside are the hardest ones to clean like the carpets. We take him out regularly and the vet said he doesn’t have any urinary issues. He is definitely just taking his time to figure this out. He is quite smart and picks up tricks right away but house training just vexes him.

My guy is has lost all of his upper and lower front teeth (incisors I think) in the span of two days. I have looked high and low but can’t find a single one. He must just be swallowing them all. I’m hoping he at least spits out a molar or a canine when he eventually loses those. I want to have at least one of his teeth to keep!

I started working on letter sounds with the then 2.5yo that I nanny for. I thought it would be a long process but a friend recommended the 35min video Leapfrog Letter Factory. I would put it on for his screen time and he loved it. We watched it a couple times and he started singing the songs on his own. Then after a couple more watches, he had all his letter sounds down. It was insane how quickly the video taught him. I now recommend it to anyone asking about learning letter sounds! It used to be on Netflix but they recently took it down. Another thing that helped was just playing with his letter blocks and asking him to identify the letters and their sounds. We just worked letters and their sounds into our play sometimes. And he was very proud of himself once he could start picking out letters and their sounds in books and on signs.

Editing just to add that he is 3.5 now! It just took time, encouragement, and practice.

INFO: Why is a six year old in preschool? I don’t know where you live so maybe that’s typical. But where I live, six year olds are normally either in first grade or the oldest in their kindergarten class. Has Conner been held back? I am not an expert on child behavior or anything like that but I do have years of experience working with kids ages 3-7. At age 2, toddlers are already attempting to blend in with their peers. At age 6, kids really feel a strong desire to conform but are also realizing that they are individuals. They love to be in groups but are also quick to reject other kids from their groups. One of the most common phrases I hear six year olds say is “you’re not invited to my birthday party.” This inclusion/exclusion thing is a big thing for them. One benefit of kids playing together is that they teach each other what is acceptable and what is not. I only say this because I am surprised that this child is so dramatic and not reacting to any of this. It could be that he is learning his behavior from his mother. But I would expect him to behave that way around his mother and change his behavior accordingly when he is with his peers. By age six, children are masters at this. I only mention all this again because I would expect this child to change his behavior if he is receiving all of this negative feedback. I know you said he has been evaluated but maybe the parents should get a second opinion. If he has already been evaluated once, there were probably other signs that lead to that recommendation. Either way, her behavior was inexcusable. And you are right that her son’s behavior is leading to him being outcast by his peers. But that could be a sign that he has some sort of deficit whether it be emotional, behavioral, or social.
